title: Qt: Expose packet flags and expert severity to accessibility
description:
Add accessibility information for packet flags (marked, ignored, ref time, modified) and expert severity levels to models.  
AI-Assisted: yes (Gemini)

Why is this required? This might lead to issues with code in the view that assumes that whatever it passes for the parent it will still return successfully. I agree that this behaviour is hacky, but should be checked before just adding this here arbitrarily.
@rknall  Do you (or anyone else) have any further thoughts about what we should do in this situation?
Let’s continue with your approach. For now it seems to be the best version for it.
Same as above, it should be checked first if other code is not relying on this behaviour.

This is intended to ensure that accessibility api knows that the list elements all have no children. Without it the child status was ambiguous until you tried to navigate. I think the accessibility API is trying to save the effort of actually looking but calls to `rowCount` are probably presumed to be cheap. The similar check in `index` is less important but is intended to mirror this one.

Thank you very much for this clarification. Let me ask you this. Are there good resources or tools that a non-impaired person could use to create a better tool that would help you right out of the gate? For instance, I've just learned that apparently screen-readers also dont read out the quotation marks around words which makes use of them to clarify something as ironic quite obsolete. The same here, this behaviour of the Qt accessibility API was unknown. But we have a few  models that do use rowCount with the parent set to a nullptr. So in that case, you would get the wrong information. I am assuming that this will especially be annoying to you, when we are using TableView models instead of ListView models like we do in this case. The reason btw is, that TableView models allow for some options in modifications that ListView models do not. 

So if there are any resources or informations that we can utilise, I would highly appreciate recommendations from you. I will also forward this info to our Discord channel as it is quite helpful. And if you ever want to reach out with questions about the program, feel free to ask me directly either on Discord or via rknall@wireshark.org. I would gladly help you in getting our program to be more accessible.

I have been struggling somewhat with the Qt accessibility resources myself. I am a previous Wireshark developer from about 2004-2005. I also built a couple of Qt apps in about 2002 and 2008. (Qt 2 and 3 as I recall). Qt accessibility has minimal documentation and few samples. (https://github.com/shoogle/accessibility-qt-chart-example is one). Since the beginning of February I have been working to improve the accessibility of Wireshark because it is a job requirement for many people in IT. My progress on the task of improving Wireshark accessibility has been limited. I have been able to markup certain elements and improve their reading by the screen reader but general navigation is still a mess for reasons that I have not been able to determine. The major views are sometimes absent, focus doesn't work reliably, and more. I will continue to pursue improvements for as long as it takes though.

I am occasionally on the discord at least a couple of times a week though I generally don't linger. Tag me there if you have further thoughts.

This works mitigating the two things above, but only if both methods above are not called directly but via the view or proxy models. And even in the case of proxy models, they might not be calling flags for every behaviour.

Agreed, I am not clear why this change isn't sufficient and I forget in which order I discovered the solutions. I will check if this change is sufficient and if index/rowCount are still called/required.
Yes, `rowCount` is still called by `hasChildren` and elsewhere. As you suggest it seems the flags are not always checked. I am not sure what a better way to handle this should be.

As I come to have a better understanding of what you are trying to achieve and especially the challenges Qt is giving you in achieving them, I think it is fine keeping it in just in case. It will not hurt and if its only purpose is to let you better utilise the application, than that is all the reasoning I need.
